question: GQ-006
method: Fetch pg<gid>.txt, measure bytes between the START and END markers, compare to the local body size.

interpretation.upstream-short: The Gutenberg plain-text file genuinely has little or no body. Our extractor was correct.
interpretation.OUR-DEFECT: Upstream has substantial text we failed to extract. This is ours to fix.
interpretation.unreachable: Fetch failed or the file has no START/END markers. Missing markers are NOT evidence of an empty body.

headline: 850 of 850 books with a local body under 8 KB byte-match their upstream Gutenberg source exactly. Zero extraction defects, zero unreachable.
supersedes: The 6-of-693 random sample from the previous loop. Six clean draws were compatible with a 1-in-100 defect rate; 850 of 850 is not.

signature_cross_check.reading: Short books average slightly shorter passages, which is expected. The maxima are near-identical, so the band shows no anomaly the corpus does not.

honest_limit: Bodies under 8 KB only — 1.1% of the corpus. A 300 KB book truncated to 200 KB would still be invisible. What is now settled is the band where truncation was plausible enough to suspect.
